title: Facilities Engineer
segmentLong: Upstream / Midstream — Surface Processing & Gathering Facilities
setting: Operations Base Office / Plant Engineering Center with regular Processing Plant and Offshore Platform walkdowns
governingStandards: GPSA Data Book; API RP 14E; API 520/521
headline: The Facilities Engineer designs, debottlenecks, and optimizes the surface processing plant, ensuring raw reservoir fluids from wellheads are safely and economically separated into marketable crude oil, sales-spec natural gas, and environmentally compliant water. While thermodynamic process simulators like Aspen HYSYS and Petro-SIM excel at steady-state phase equilibrium and column hydraulics, they function as static design silos detached from live field operations. In maturing fields, water cuts surge from 15% to 80% and gas-oil ratios swing wildly, but evaluating whether existing 3-phase separators provide sufficient liquid retention time or if gathering headers exceed API RP 14E erosional velocity limits is still performed using manual, fragmented Excel spreadsheets. Facilities engineers spend over 45% of their working hours manually pulling SCADA trends, searching for equipment design datasheets in legacy archives, and recalculating vessel retention times. A hyper-specialized agent squad eliminates 39.00 hours per engineering surveillance and project cycle across separator capacity sieving, plant mass balancing, piping erosional velocity audits, TEG dehydration optimization, electrostatic treater diagnostics, water train compliance, and tie-in debottlenecking.

role.oneLine: Designs, debottlenecks, and optimizes surface production processing facilities (slug catchers, 3-phase separators, electrostatic heater treaters, TEG gas dehydration skids, produced water hydrocyclones, and flare relief networks) to treat raw reservoir fluids into commercial sales products.
role.whyItMatters: Flawed surface facility engineering causes catastrophic separator liquid carryover into gas compressors (causing explosive impeller destruction), oil carryunder into produced water overboard streams violating environmental permits, or undersized flare relief headers overpressuring vessels during emergency depressurizations.

variants.name: Offshore Topside Facilities Engineer
variants.detail: Manages extreme space/weight-constrained equipment footprints, compact cyclonic separators, electrostatic coalescers, subsea tie-in reception manifolds, and structural deck limits.

variants.name: Onshore Central Processing Facility (CPF) Engineer
variants.detail: Manages large-footprint separation batteries, massive produced water disposal skids, heavy oil thermal steam generation (SAGD/CSS), and field gathering networks.

variants.name: Unconventional Shale Battery Engineer
variants.detail: Manages standardized modular production skids, high-velocity sand knockouts, vapor recovery towers (VRT), and fluctuating tank battery vapor emissions.

role.titleCheck: The industry title is Facilities Engineer or Surface Process Engineer. Avoid confusing this role with "Refinery Process Engineer" (who works on downstream fractional distillation and catalytic cracking units) or "Civil/Structural Engineer" (who designs module steel and foundations).

whereTheWorkHappens.Work Setting: Operations Base Office / Plant Engineering Center: Professional engineering workstation environment with regular walkdowns across hot, noisy processing modules, separator banks, and compressor shelters.
whereTheWorkHappens.What They Can Reach: Multi-screen workstation running process simulation software (Aspen HYSYS, Petro-SIM), equipment sizing spreadsheets, CAD P&ID viewers, and plant SCADA historians (OSIsoft PI).
whereTheWorkHappens.Shift Pattern: Standard professional engineering office hours (08:00–17:00), with intensive 24/7 on-site presence during plant turnarounds (TAR), equipment commissioning, and major tie-in campaigns.
whereTheWorkHappens.Where the Record Lives: Corporate Equipment Design Datasheets, Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), Aspen HYSYS simulation models, and Management of Change (MOC) dossiers.

standards.citation: [GPSA-DataBook]: Gas Processors Suppliers Association, GPSA Engineering Data Book, 14th Edition. The global authority on gas and liquid surface processing.
[API-RP-14E]: American Petroleum Institute, Recommended Practice for Design and Installation of Offshore Production Platform Piping Systems, 5th Edition.
[API-RP-520-521]: American Petroleum Institute, Sizing, Selection, and Installation of Pressure-Relieving Devices (520) & Guide for Pressure-Relieving and Depressuring Systems (521).
[SPE-Facilities]: Society of Petroleum Engineers, Competency Management Tool: Projects, Facilities, and Construction Discipline Matrix.
[NACE-MR0175]: NACE International / ISO 15156, Petroleum and natural gas industries — Materials for use in H2S-containing environments in oil and gas production.
[API-MPMS-Ch20]: American Petroleum Institute, Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards, Chapter 20 — Production Allocation Measurement.

vendorGaps.solves: Rigorous thermodynamic phase equilibrium, equation-of-state fluid modeling, heat exchanger rating, and distillation column hydraulics.
vendorGaps.gap: Static simulation silo. Requires manual configuration of feed compositions and conditions. It cannot pull live SCADA data to audit real-time equipment design margins or autonomously flag separating capacity bottlenecks.

vendorGaps.solves: Multi-source flare header network backpressure modeling and sonic choke evaluation during emergency blowdown.
vendorGaps.gap: Used for design and periodic re-validation; completely disconnected from day-to-day flaring reconciliation and live separator mass balances.

vendorGaps.solves: High-frequency logging of plant temperatures, pressures, vessel liquid levels, and flowmeter rates.
vendorGaps.gap: Stores raw time-series data without physical equipment geometry (vessel diameter, length, weir height, nozzle schedule) to calculate retention times or droplet settling velocities.

vendorGaps.solves: Houses vendor equipment drawings, certified fabrication datasheets, and manufacturer pump curves.
vendorGaps.gap: Unstructured PDF storage. Engineers must spend hours digging through folders to locate the weir height or mist extractor design velocity of a 1995 production vessel.

actions.action: Audit 3-phase production separator liquid retention times and capacity limits
actions.label: Separator Capacity & Retention Time Audit (B1, [GPSA-DataBook §7])
actions.today: Engineer spends hours gathering vessel dimensions from paper equipment datasheets and extracting monthly flowrates to manually calculate oil/water residence times in Excel.
actions.failureMode: Unnoticed retention time shortfalls cause poor oil-water separation, overloading downstream water treatment and violating crude sales BS&W specs.
actions.agentNote: → See §4 (Agent 1: 3-Phase Separator Retention Time & Liquid Capacity Sieve).

actions.action: Reconcile daily plant mass and energy balance across all process trains
actions.label: Plant Mass & Energy Balance Reconciliation (B1, [SPE-Facilities §2])
actions.today: Engineer manually aligns inlet multiphase meters against crude oil export, gas pipeline sales, flare meters, and produced water overboard discharge in spreadsheets.
actions.failureMode: Persistent mass balance imbalances (>5%) obscure unmeasured hydrocarbon venting, flare meter drift, or underground gathering line leaks.
actions.agentNote: → See §4 (Agent 2: Plant Hydrocarbon Mass & Energy Balance Reconciler).

actions.action: Size relief valves (PSVs) and audit flare header hydraulic backpressures
actions.label: PSV Sizing & Flare Header Hydraulics (B2, [API-RP-520-521])
actions.today: Handled inside specialized software (Aspen Flare System Analyzer, HYSYS). The engineer models fire, blocked discharge, and tube rupture scenarios.
actions.agentNote: ❌ No. Critical process safety calculation. The monolith owns the relief hydraulics; certified human engineers must approve PSV orifice areas.

actions.action: Evaluate erosional velocity limits on facility piping using API RP 14E
actions.label: Piping Erosional Velocity Evaluation (B1, [API-RP-14E §2])
actions.today: Engineer manually calculates API RP 14E mixture velocities for dozens of pipe segments whenever production rates or GORs increase.
actions.failureMode: Operating above erosional velocity limits causes severe sand washouts, pipe wall thinning, and catastrophic loss of primary containment.
actions.agentNote: → See §4 (Agent 3: API RP 14E Piping Erosional Velocity & Sand Risk Sieve).

actions.action: Audit gas dehydration triethylene glycol (TEG) circulation and reboiler duty
actions.label: TEG Dehydration Glycol Optimization (B1, [GPSA-DataBook §20])
actions.today: Engineer calculates water removal and reboiler heat duty once every six months; changes in gas flow or inlet temperature lead to off-spec wet gas.
actions.failureMode: Excessive glycol loss (>0.1 gal/MMSCF) costs tens of thousands in chemical waste; under-dehydrated gas causes pipeline hydrate blockages.
actions.agentNote: → See §4 (Agent 4: Gas Dehydration TEG Contactor & Reboiler Health Diagnostic Agent).

actions.action: Troubleshoot electrostatic treater/desalter grid tripping and rag-layer buildup
actions.label: Electrostatic Treater & Rag-Layer Troubleshooting (B1, [GPSA-DataBook §8])
actions.today: Engineer reviews desalter transformer current logs only after the grid trips on over-current, shutting down export crude treatment.
actions.failureMode: Rag-layer emulsion accumulation bridges the high-voltage grids, causing immediate power trips and thousands of barrels of off-spec wet oil.
actions.agentNote: → See §4 (Agent 5: Electrostatic Treater & Desalter Rag-Layer Tripping Diagnostic Agent).

actions.action: Screen produced water treatment skids (hydrocyclones, IGF) for OIW compliance
actions.label: Produced Water Treatment Skid Screening (B1, [SPE-Facilities §3])
actions.today: Engineer checks daily water lab logs; hydrocyclone liner fouling and IGF flotation efficiency loss are caught only after overboard discharge spikes.
actions.failureMode: Out-of-spec oil-in-water (>29 ppm) breaches statutory environmental permits, risking mandatory regulatory platform shut-in.
actions.agentNote: → See §4 (Agent 6: Produced Water Hydrocyclone & IGF Flotation Compliance Sieve).

actions.action: Screen facility equipment constraints for new field development tie-in studies
actions.label: Field Tie-In Debottlenecking Studies (B1, [SPE-Facilities §1])
actions.today: Evaluating an upcoming 5-well tie-in requires the engineer to manually cross-reference 40 pieces of surface equipment to identify which vessel hits capacity first.
actions.failureMode: Unidentified bottlenecks (e.g., produced water disposal pump capacity) stall field start-up, delaying production ramp-up by months.
actions.agentNote: → See §4 (Agent 7: Facility Debottlenecking & New Well Tie-In Capacity Sieve).

actions.action: Author technical equipment procurement datasheets for vessels and pumps
actions.label: Authoring Technical Equipment Procurement Datasheets (B2, [SPE-Facilities §4])
actions.today: Writing detailed engineering procurement specifications for new pressure vessels, shell-and-tube exchangers, and pumps.
actions.agentNote: ❌ No. Governed by EPC project engineering teams and senior project engineering staff.

agents.name: 3-Phase Separator Retention Time & Liquid Capacity Sieve
agents.oneLine: Continuously cross-references live SCADA production flows against vessel internal geometry to calculate oil/water retention times and warn of impending liquid carryover.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 4.50 hours per capacity audit of manual equipment datasheet searching, fluid property lookups, and vessel sizing mathematics.
agents.reads: Inlet multi-stream flowmeters (Qoil, Qwater, Qgas), vessel operating temperature and pressure, fluid laboratory densities and viscosities, and vessel design specs from equipment datasheets (inside diameter, seam-to-seam length, weir heights, mist extractor type).
agents.does: Calculates actual liquid residence times (tres = racVliquidQliquid) for oil and water phases against GPSA Section 7 criteria (minimum 3–5 min for light crude, 10–20 min for heavy/viscous crude); computes gas phase Souders-Brown terminal settling velocity (vmax = K sqrt rac hoL - hog hog); models droplet settling paths to detect impending liquid carryover into gas outlets or water carryunder into oil compartments.
agents.returns: Separator Operating Envelope & Capacity Margin Dossier (vessel_id, actual_oil_retention_min, actual_water_retention_min, gas_velocity_ratio, hydraulic_capacity_margin_pct, carryover_risk_alert).
agents.stopsAt: Overwriting vessel operating setpoints in the DCS or authorizing physical weir plate modifications.
agents.failureModes: If vessel liquid level transmitters read below interface weir elevation, the agent tags the audit as [Abnormal Level Control — Residence Time Model Suspended].

agents.name: Plant Hydrocarbon Mass & Energy Balance Reconciler
agents.oneLine: Solves continuous 24-hour conservation-of-mass equations across plant processing trains to isolate metering drift, unrecorded venting, and gathering line leaks.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 1.75 hours daily of pulling multi-meter spreadsheets and manually untangling plant balance imbalances.
agents.reads: Inlet manifold multiphase meters, high-pressure and test separator liquid/gas meters, crude export LACT meters, sales gas ultrasonic meters, fuel gas consumers, and flare stack meters.
agents.does: Solves daily mass conservation equations across all plant processing nodes; isolates mass balance closure errors (Δm = Inlet - sum Exports); identifies meter drift or unmetered losses exceeding API MPMS Chapter 20 tolerances (±2%); isolates whether discrepancy is gas phase (venting/metering) or liquid phase (pipeline loss/tank strapping error).
agents.returns: Daily Facility Mass Balance Reconciliation Dossier (facility_id, total_inlet_mass_tonnes, total_export_mass_tonnes, balance_closure_pct, suspect_meter_tags, unaccounted_loss_allocation).
agents.stopsAt: Committing official corporate production accounting volumes to regulatory portals.
agents.failureModes: If un-reconciled mass imbalance exceeds 5% continuously for 48 hours, the agent issues a high-priority advisory: [Major Facility Mass Imbalance — Immediate Fugitive Loss & Meter Audit Required].

agents.name: API RP 14E Piping Erosional Velocity & Sand Risk Sieve
agents.oneLine: Evaluates facility gathering headers and manifold piping against API RP 14E erosional velocity thresholds to identify accelerated erosion-corrosion failure risks.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 3.65 hours per gathering header audit of manual multiphase mixture density and velocity calculations.
agents.reads: Piping line schedules (nominal diameter, wall thickness, metallurgy schedule), flowing pressures, temperatures, gas and liquid mass flowrates, and acoustic sand detector telemetry.
agents.does: Solves API RP 14E erosional velocity equations: ve = raccsqrt hom(wherec = 100for solids-free continuous flow /125for intermittent flow per API 14E, or deratedc = 150-200for CRA alloys); computes actual multiphase mixture velocity (vm); calculates Erosional Velocity Ratio (EVR = vm / ve); cross-references with sand rate telemetry to flag pipe elbows operating at accelerated wall thinning risk (EVR > 0.80).
agents.returns: Piping Segment Erosional Risk Register (line_id, mixture_velocity_fps, erosional_velocity_fps, evr_ratio, critical_erosion_flag, recommended_ultrasonic_ndt_inspection_points).
agents.stopsAt: Altering well choke operating setpoints or re-rating piping ANSI pressure classes.
agents.failureModes: If any piping line segment exhibits an EVR ≥1.0, the agent triggers an immediate alert: [Critical API RP 14E Exceedance — Piping Wall Thinning Hazard].

agents.name: Gas Dehydration TEG Contactor & Reboiler Health Diagnostic Agent
agents.oneLine: Analyzes triethylene glycol (TEG) circulation rates, reboiler thermal duties, and dry gas moisture to eliminate chemical glycol losses and prevent pipeline hydrate blockages.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 3.15 hours weekly of manual dehydration balance calculations, preventing costly chemical losses and off-spec sales gas.
agents.reads: Wet gas inlet flow, pressure, and temperature, dry gas moisture content (lb H2O / MMSCF), lean and rich glycol circulation rates (GPM), reboiler temperature, and glycol flash separator pressures.
agents.does: Evaluates water removal efficiency per GPSA Section 20; audits glycol circulation ratio (gal TEG / lb H2O removed, typically 2.5–4.0 gal/lb); monitors reboiler thermal heat duty and stripping gas efficiency; detects excessive glycol carryover or contactor foaming (>0.1 gal/MMSCF); flags high water dew points risking downstream pipeline hydrate formation.
agents.returns: TEG Contactor & Dehydration Performance Card (train_id, water_dewpoint_spec_status, glycol_circulation_ratio, glycol_loss_rate_gal_per_mmscf, reboiler_fouling_index, recommended_reboiler_duty_trim).
agents.stopsAt: Adjusting burner fuel gas control valves or altering glycol circulation pump VFD setpoints.
agents.failureModes: If reboiler temperature exceeds 404°F (206.7°C), the agent flags [TEG Thermal Decomposition Alarm — Reduce Reboiler Firing Immediately].

agents.name: Electrostatic Treater & Desalter Rag-Layer Tripping Diagnostic Agent
agents.oneLine: Monitors electrostatic desalter and heater treater transformer electrical loads and emulsion interfaces to predict rag-layer grid shorts before export crude trips.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 2.70 hours per treater upset of manual log sifting, preventing off-spec wet crude export and emergency vessel shutdowns.
agents.reads: Crude emulsion inlet temperature, water cut, chemical demulsifier injection rates (ppm), electrostatic transformer secondary voltage and amperage, interface level transmitter (ILT) readings, and crude export BS&W.
agents.does: Tracks transformer electrical power characteristics; detects conductive emulsion rag-layer formation (interface accumulation of asphaltenes, clays, and micro-droplets) that bridges high-voltage grids; calculates chemical demulsifier treating efficiency vs water separation rate; warns of impending electrical grid collapse/tripping before vessel trips.
agents.returns: Electrostatic Treater Health & Rag-Layer Advisory (treater_id, grid_current_ma, rag_layer_thickness_estimate_in, transformer_trip_risk_score, demulsifier_ppm_optimization_target, interface_drain_action_advisory).
agents.stopsAt: Commanding vessel interface dump valves or resetting transformer circuit breakers.
agents.failureModes: If transformer secondary current spikes >85% of overload rating, the agent triggers an emergency advisory: [Imminent Electrostatic Grid Short — Manual Interface Flush Recommended].

agents.name: Produced Water Hydrocyclone & IGF Flotation Compliance Sieve
agents.oneLine: Evaluates produced water hydrocyclone pressure drop ratios and induced gas flotation (IGF) performance to maintain strict environmental discharge compliance.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 2.25 hours per surveillance cycle of cross-referencing water treatment parameters against environmental discharge permits.
agents.reads: Water treatment skid inlet flow, hydrocyclone pressure drop ratio (PDR), induced gas flotation (IGF) vessel pressure and gas shroud rates, chemical coagulant/de-oiler dosing, and online/lab Oil-in-Water (OIW) concentrations.
agents.does: Evaluates hydrocyclone separation efficiency against inlet fluid shearing; audits IGF micro-bubble sparging performance; computes cumulative oil removal efficiency across the entire water train; forecasts overboard exceedance or disposal well pore-throat plugging risks (>50 ppm OIW or excessive TSS).
agents.returns: Produced Water Train Quality & Environmental Compliance Ledger (skid_id, pdr_actual_vs_target, igf_removal_efficiency_pct, disposal_well_plugging_risk, overboard_regulatory_margin_ppm, chemical_coagulant_trim_advisory).
agents.stopsAt: Actuating overboard divert valves to slop tanks or changing disposal well injection permits.
agents.failureModes: If online OIW exceeds 29 ppm offshore statutory limit, the agent triggers an immediate red banner: [Environmental Compliance Alert — Overboard Discharge Limit Approaching].

agents.name: Facility Debottlenecking & New Well Tie-In Capacity Sieve
agents.oneLine: Simultaneously stress-tests 40+ pieces of surface processing equipment against new well development profiles to map hydraulic bottlenecks and rank debottlenecking options.
agents.frictionSolved: Eliminates 21.00 hours per field development tie-in study of cross-referencing multi-vessel capacity curves and authoring debottlenecking reports.
agents.reads: Planned new well tie-in production forecast curves (Qoil, Qwater, Qgas over 3-year horizon), complete facility equipment design master registers (separators, heat exchangers, pumps, compressors, water treaters, flare lines), and active operating constraint envelopes.
agents.does: Performs automated hydraulic and thermodynamic rating checks across all 40+ surface processing components simultaneously; maps the critical bottleneck equipment item that chokes production for each phase (e.g. "Produced water booster pump P-102 hits 100% capacity at Month 4, limiting asset oil to 14,200 bopd"); models cost-effective debottlenecking options (e.g., pump impeller up-sizing vs piping bypass).
agents.returns: Comprehensive Facility Tie-In Debottlenecking Dossier (project_id, maximum_constrained_oil_rate_bopd, limiting_bottleneck_tag, constraint_timeline_months, recommended_debottlenecking_modifications_ranked_by_cost_efficiency).
agents.stopsAt: Approving capital AFE project budgets or authoring official MOC approvals.
agents.failureModes: If tie-in production introduces high H2S into a facility constructed with standard carbon steel piping, the agent issues a critical metallurgy violation: [NACE MR0175 Sour Service Incompatibility — Sulfide Stress Cracking Risk].

line: "A facilities engineer shouldn't spend three days looking for the internal diameter of a 1982 production separator in a paper archive; their job is ensuring the facility can handle another ten thousand barrels of fluid without blowing oil out the flare stack."
openQuestions: How often is well production choked back in the field simply because an engineer hasn't had time to verify whether the downstream separator can handle the extra water cut?
What is the average discrepancy between upstream well allocation meters and the fiscal sales export meters at the facility boundary?
